title: Convert binary floating values with bounded integer storage
problem: Device environments cannot consistently provide host conversion services.
design: Representation bits drive classification and exact interval comparisons. Bounded integer limbs hold decimal expansions without output-capacity limits.
tradeoffs: Integer interval conversion uses more code and bounded working storage than forwarding to libc, while avoiding locale and allocation services. Internal conversion renders supported finite magnitudes; the formatting layer handles signs and nonfinite spellings. The documented 1100/16520-digit bounds cover exact IEEE expansions and interval endpoints, rather than limiting requested output precision. Direct oracle tests cover adjacent powers of two, subnormal/normal transitions, maximum finite values, rounding ties and carries.
